subject: Evaluation instrumentation & SLO definition — next steps for Ava Solutions trial
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Thompson <samantha.thompson@avasolutions.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation instrumentation & SLO definition — next steps for Ava Solutions trial

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed measurement-first plan so we can move toward a scoped trial that proves the two things you said matter most: latency/cost predictability for your search-augmentation use case, and end-to-end extraction accuracy on domain documents.

High-level objective
- Run a 3-week trial that validates Redwood inference can meet your latency SLOs under representative load while keeping per-token cost within your target band, and that our model/serving configuration meets your extraction quality targets on your sample prompt set.

Proposed success criteria (measurable) — please confirm these are aligned:
- Latency: P95 inference latency <= 250 ms for 4k-context generative extraction flows; P99 <= 500 ms for peak windows.
- Throughput: Sustained throughput of 60 requests/sec with tail latency still within SLO; autoscaling should handle 2x bursts for 10 minutes.
- Cost: End-to-end inference unit cost <= $0.0016 per token avg (token accounting includes generation + model context); daily cost variance < 15%.
- Quality: Extraction accuracy (field-level F1) >= 92% on your labeled holdout; hallucination incidence < 1% for knowledge checks; average human rating >= 4.2/5 on the 100-sample human eval set.

Instrumentation & data to collect (we will provide dashboards):
- Token-level usage, model variant, quantization profile, and batching metrics (tokens/sec, avg batch size).
- Per-request traces with KV cache hit/miss, prefill vs generation token split, and GPU utilization.
- Error/retry breakdown and failed-output samples (redacted for PII).

Ownership & roles
- Redwood: Ben Carter (SE) will configure the trial cluster, sample-inference-config.yaml attached, and stand up the dashboards; Neha Kapoor will own any security/data-handling questions.
- Ava Solutions: Samantha to own dataset labeling and access to a 2k-sample labeled holdout + 100 human-eval samples; Tom to coordinate procurement/POC sign-off.

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (Nov 30–Dec 4): NDA/POC statement of work signed; data access & redaction rules exchanged.
- Week 1 (Dec 7–11): Redwood staging deployment + sample-config applied; smoke tests with 200 synthetic queries.
- Week 2 (Dec 14–18): Full-run with your 2k sample set; metric collection and initial quality eval.
- Week 3 (Dec 21–23): Human eval scoring + final report and recommendation.

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) Samantha: confirm the labeled holdout availability and any PII redaction requirements by EOD Mon (Nov 30).
2) Tom: can you confirm budget holder and target PO timeline so we can issue the POC SOW?
3) Ben (SE): will produce sample runbooks and the trial cluster config by Monday.

Attachments: avas_trial_scope_v1.pdf (scope + SOW template), sample-inference-config.yaml (example), redaction_requirements.docx (form).

If that looks good I’ll slot a 30-minute kickoff for Mon Dec 7 at 10:00 PT.

Thanks —
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference
From: Samantha Thompson <samantha.thompson@avasolutions.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@avasolutions.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation instrumentation & SLO definition — next steps for Ava Solutions trial

Thanks Soojin — great summary and thanks to Ben and Neha for joining. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The labeled holdout (2,000 records) exists but ~12% contain PII that our legal team requires redaction for. I’ll send the redaction spec by EOD Mon; if Redwood can accept pre-redacted pulls that’s ideal.
- On cost: our internal target is closer to $0.0012/token at scale — I know that’s aggressive, but we’d like to see what batching + quantization profile you recommend. Can the trial produce cost breakdowns per model variant?
- Quality: we can provide the 100 human-eval samples by Dec 11. We also want a few representative long-context examples (4k tokens) — will that be supported in staging?

We’re generally aligned on the timeline; confirming availability for Dec 7 kickoff at 10:00 PT. One ask: can Ben share a short checklist of the network/IP ranges your staging will use so our infra team can whitelist?

Samantha
Director, Applied AI — Ava Solutions
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Thompson <samantha.thompson@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation instrumentation & SLO definition — next steps for Ava Solutions trial

Samantha — thanks, that helps. Quick answers inline and a few clarifications: 

- PII/redaction: we can accept pre-redacted pulls. Neha, copying you to confirm the redaction checklist and whether we need a separate data ingestion enclave.
- Cost breakdown by model variant: yes — dashboards will show per-variant tokens, avg cost/token, and a projected monthlyized cost at the observed qps. We’ll include both raw token accounting and estimated infra amortized cost.
- Long-context support: staging will be configured to 4k context for the trial; sample-inference-config.yaml shows the selected model and kv-cache settings.
- Network whitelisting: Ben will follow up with IP ranges and a short allowlist checklist.

Confirming kickoff: Mon Dec 7, 10:00 PT. I’ll send a calendar invite and Ben will attach the checklist + runbook.

Ben / Neha — action items:
- Ben: send IP ranges + runbook + staging endpoint by Monday morning (Dec 1).
- Neha: review redaction_requirements.docx and advise if a separate enclave is needed; provide minimum audit log retention requirements.

We’ll keep the DocuSign POC SOW in parallel; Tom, if you can share who will sign that we’ll accelerate.

Best,
Soojin
